api-answers:
&api-questions;
The nbfx Shell API is the product-facing contract of the generic JavaFX application shell: the window facade and pane/tab manager, pane roles and hosts, the chrome and branding contracts, the UI-ready hook, the window-environment capabilities, the shutdown contract and the pane-provider SPI, the window-system lifecycle and its WindowSink/WindowState model, plus CJAP declarative shell-region metadata, provider/frame contracts and region-host lifecycle. The shell implementation is nbfx.platform.shell.
A product implements the chrome/branding/window-environment contracts or registers a WindowPaneProvider; nbfx.platform.shell composes them and publishes the running window as ShellWindow and WindowManager. The API knows no project, IDE or Java type; editor documents and project state are resolved by the contribution through its lookup.
Product-facing shell contracts, including Node-free CJAP region metadata. This API remains devel until the CJAP reference product and scenarios pass.
Shell shutdown coordination contracts. This API remains devel until the CJAP reference product and scenarios pass.
Shell pane-provider SPI. This API remains devel until the CJAP reference product and scenarios pass.
A product replaces the application name, title, icons and stylesheets with ShellBranding.
A product supplies top/bottom chrome with ShellChromeProvider.
A product registers a permanent pane with WindowPaneProvider and moves tabs through WindowManager.
A product adds a shutdown participant with ShutdownParticipant.
An @OnUiReady task reaches the window through ShellWindowProvider.
A product declares shell chrome slots with @ShellRegionRegistration and reads immutable metadata through ShellRegionRegistry.
A product contributes fresh per-shell Nodes with @ShellContributionRegistration; metadata discovery never constructs classes or Nodes.
A product supplies a ShellProvider/ShellFrame while the runtime owns region mounting, update and disposal through ShellRegionHost.
PaneRoleTest covers the canonical roles and the product-role rules. The shell modules exercise the contracts in their unit tests and the AppShell conformance fixture. The API is under development until the MVP freeze, after which signature tests (sigtest) are enabled. CJAP region tests cover id/kind canonicalization, immutable specs, direct-folder discovery, profile filtering, malformed/duplicate isolation and generated layer equality. Contribution tests cover loader-free metadata discovery, strict attributes, profile filtering before construction, fresh per-shell instances and DOCK exclusion. Frame API tests cover profile ids, context validation and optional renderer disposal.
A JDK is required to compile; JavaFX is provided by the runtime.
org.netbeans.api.nbfx.shell, org.netbeans.api.nbfx.shell.shutdown and org.netbeans.spi.nbfx.shell are exported. The implementation packages of nbfx.platform.shell are not.
ShellWindowProvider, the chrome/branding providers, the window-environment capabilities and WindowPaneProvider are resolved from the shell lookup; @OnUiReady is a named service under NbFx/UIReady.
The host module registers its implementations; this module only defines the contracts. @ServiceProvider(service = Processor.class) registers ShellRegionRegistrationProcessor and ShellContributionRegistrationProcessor at compile time.
@ShellRegionRegistration writes direct region metadata folders under NbFx/ShellRegions. Direct .instance children may declare ShellContribution implementations; nested menu/action folders are not region or contribution metadata.
ShellRegionRegistry reads direct region folders. ShellContributionRegistry reads direct class-based .instance children through LayerInstances and never uses DataObject, DataNode or InstanceCookie. It performs no implicit filesystem or network access.
None.
Window and scene-graph operations run on the JavaFX Application Thread. The shutdown confirmation runs on that thread, while the selected cleanup runs off it. CJAP region ids, specs, annotation processing and metadata discovery are Node-free and stateless. Contribution construction creates fresh per-shell instances. Provider/frame creation and region mount/update/dispose run on the JavaFX Application Thread under the runtime mount owner's lifecycle.
No code runs on startup; the contracts are resolved when the shell starts.
No code runs on exit beyond the registered shutdown participants.
No special requirements.
